lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The floor keeps dropping out beneath Toronto - and Thursday's defeat made the basement visible. The Maple Leafs fell 5-2 to Minnesota, their fourth straight loss and fifth consecutive regulation defeat at home, leaving them 8-11, 12th in the Eastern Conference with 18 points and 10 games out. Auston Matthews finally scored his first goal of November, but even the captain admitted confidence has been shaken. Zack MacEwen supplied a goal and an assist, a useful spark from the fourth line, yet the larger problem remains on the blue line: Morgan Rielly is sidelined with a lower-body injury, while Chris Tanev was scratched for maintenance against the Wild. This is no longer a brief wobble; it is a team misplacing its identity in broad daylight. Edmonton arrives Saturday at 7 p.m. ET on Sportsnet - the Leafs need urgency, structure and a response before this slump hardens into their season.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays left Las Vegas without a transaction, but not without a blueprint. Ross Atkins said Toronto held more than 100 conversations with agents and clubs and came away more confident about the market - a useful start, not a finished offseason. The needs are unmistakable: rotation depth after an injury-riddled year, bullpen flexibility, and a middle-of-the-order jolt. Kevin Gausman's possible return would bring credibility and innings; Jazz Chisholm Jr. would bring electricity, versatility and the sort of offensive pressure this roster needs. Spencer Miles' 95.2-inning rookie season also gives Toronto an intriguing internal lever, though Atkins wisely wants more workload with less role volatility. The final record was -2.0 points, but that number belongs in the rearview mirror. Now watch whether Toronto turns its GM-meeting confidence into an infield deal or a rotation commitment before camp opens March 25 at Yankee Stadium.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors are discovering how thin the margin becomes when the stars sit and the schedule turns cruel. Toronto fell 123-112 to Philadelphia on Thursday, its third straight loss, despite a spirited response from RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley. Barrett delivered 31 points and 14 rebounds; Quickley added 25, but the short-handed Raptors could not contain Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid. Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard remained out, and their absences now define the club's problems more than any promising offensive burst. At 5-7, Toronto sits fourth in the Atlantic Division, five games behind, with a minus-1.0 points mark - respectable enough to stay within sight, but not sturdy enough to ignore the skid. The Celtics loss two nights earlier only sharpened the concern. Sunday's 6 p.m. ET meeting with the Knicks is the next test: Toronto must defend with purpose and prove Barrett and Quickley can carry more than a scoring burden.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The season did not die Thursday night - it staggered off the canvas, bloodied but breathing. Stefon Diggs' 32-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels with 57 seconds left lifted Washington over the Giants, 24-21, a rescue mission after Daniels threw two fourth-quarter interceptions. Diggs finished with six catches for 83 yards, while Daniels delivered three touchdown passes and enough nerve to survive his messiest stretch of the season. The Commanders are 3-5-1, third in the NFC East and two games behind New York, but this was more than a win - it was a tiebreaker and a pulse. Tight end Chig Okonkwo left with a back injury but returned after halftime, an encouraging sign in an otherwise costly night. Now comes the pause before Cincinnati visits Washington on Nov. 23 - the Bengals game will show whether this revival has legs.

article.title: Commanders Beat Giants on Diggs Touchdown
paragraphs: The Washington Commanders found a late answer Thursday, beating the Giants 24-21 when Jayden Daniels hit Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. Daniels finished with 249 passing yards and three touchdowns, while Diggs had 83 receiving yards and a score. Washington is 3-5-1 and hosts Cincinnati on Monday, November 23.

The Leafs had no such finish, losing 5-2 to Minnesota at home. Auston Matthews scored, Zack MacEwen had a goal and an assist, and Anthony Stolarz made 21 saves. Toronto is 8-11 and visits the Oilers Saturday at 7:00 p.m. ET on Sportsnet.

The Raptors fell 123-112 to Philadelphia despite RJ Barrett's 31 points and 14 rebounds; Immanuel Quickley added six assists. Toronto faces the Knicks Sunday at 6:00 p.m. The Jays are looking ahead to the Yankees, with the regular season opening March 25 at 1:35 p.m. ET in New York.
